_readme: RFC-0063 bench baseline — the reference min-times `vyrn bench --compare`
measures regressions against. JSON has no comments, so this doc lives in
the ignored `_readme`/`placeholder` fields (the comparator reads only
`benches`).
THIS IS STILL A PLACEHOLDER. `placeholder: true` (and the empty `benches`)
makes `--compare` report every bench as `new` and exit 0 — comparing real
timings against an unseeded baseline is meaningless, never a failure. The
CI bench job is a real gate now (it no longer carries `continue-on-error`),
and it stays a no-op until this file is seeded, by this arithmetic and not
by a flag.
SEEDING IT. Take the numbers from CI hardware, never from a dev machine:
comparing across machines is noise, not a measurement. The `benchmarks
(regression gate)` job of the CI workflow, on a push to main, assembles
exactly this document and uploads it. Seeding is two commands:
1. Open the newest green `CI` run on main, download the `bench-json`
artifact (it holds one report per bench-bearing example PLUS the
merged `baseline.json`).
2. cp baseline.json bench/baseline.json && git commit
The merged file has no `placeholder` and no `_readme`, so committing it
arms the gate in the same commit. There is nothing to hand-edit — the shape
is produced by the `Assemble a seedable baseline` step, and hand-merging
the per-example reports is what that step exists to prevent.
Refresh the same way whenever the runner hardware changes, and record which
workflow run the numbers came from in the commit message.
The failure margin is NOT here. It is `BENCH_THRESHOLD` in
.github/workflows/ci.yml, one value with its justification beside it.
Local refresh on a quiet machine (smoke-testing only, do NOT commit):
vyrn bench examples/benching.vyrn --json > bench/baseline.json
